scene_delivery_policy now closes an unregistered delivery surface fail-closed: _select_surface_policy returns a registered-but-closed policy (source=unregistered_closed, closed=true) and filter_delivery_scenes excludes the whole request with REASON_SCENE_SURFACE_UNREGISTERED. The only opening is the P1 development bypass hook smart_core_surface_unregistered_bypass (smart_construction_core/core_extension_surface_bypass.py): runtime env required, stage in {dev,test,local,stage,staging}, the caller must resolve as a platform administrator through smart_core.security.platform_admin.user_is_platform_admin (the identity the runtime contract publishes as identity.is_platform_admin); bypass hits are marked surface_policy_bypass=true in nav_meta.delivery_policy. No capability key, ACL widening or customer role added. Boundary documented in docs/architecture/backend_scene_surface_authority_boundary_v1.md section 7.1 and pinned (negative-first) by verify.backend.scene_surface_boundary.unit.

The unregistered-surface closure ships with one authorized escape hatch so development can still reach a surface the product has not registered. P0 (scene_delivery_policy) only asks the extension hook smart_core_surface_unregistered_bypass and never decides the role. P1 (smart_construction_core/core_extension_surface_bypass.py) grants it only when (1) a runtime env exists, (2) the runtime stage is in {dev,test,local,stage,staging}, (3) the caller is a platform administrator, consumed through smart_core.security.platform_admin.user_is_platform_admin - the same identity the runtime contract publishes as identity.is_platform_admin. Corrected this round: the first cut authorized a 'system_admin' role code that IdentityResolver can never produce (its vocabulary is executive/pm/finance/project_member), which made the escape hatch dead; verified live in sc_dev_demo that platform admin (admin) is admitted on dev and denied on prod, and a non-admin user is denied. No capability key, no ACL widening, no customer role; production stays closed.

addons/smart_core/tests/test_scene_delivery_policy.py (delivery-filter runtime semantics) is not collected: addons/smart_core/tests/__init__.py never imports it (git log -S shows it was never wired since the clean baseline). It also calls filter_delivery_scenes without env, so the P1 policy-file/alias hooks (smart_core_surface_policy_file_default, smart_core_surface_aliases) are unreachable and 2 of its 6 cases assert a degenerate path that fails on HEAD too (verified by stashing scene_delivery_policy.py back to HEAD: same 2 failures). Wiring it in requires an owning-layer decision on whether a smart_core test may depend on the P1 hook; until then it is not evidence. The boundary doc now states this explicitly instead of citing the file as runtime evidence.

local.dev.health failed frontend_http=403 while /web/login and /api/runtime-version were 200. Root cause: nginx bind-mounts frontend/apps/web/dist-dev, and that host directory was recreated today (13:03) by the static build, so the running nginx container still pointed at the removed inode and saw an empty html root (index.html absent -> 403). Not caused by any code change. Repaired through the governed local.dev.down + local.dev.up (volumes preserved); local.dev.health now PASS and GET / returns 200. Recurrence note for the ops owner: scripts/dev/restart.sh force-recreates only odoo, so a recreated dist-dev needs a full down/up (or an extended restart wrapper) before the preview serves the new build.

backend_scene_surface_boundary_unit.detail: locks the scene/surface boundary: closed exclusion-reason vocabulary, fail-closed allowlist for a registered delivery surface, fail-closed + SCENE_SURFACE_UNREGISTERED exclusion for an unregistered surface, and the development bypass.
